messages.subject: Re: Random site effect on occupancy blowing up
parts:
Dear Matt,

is this a static (a.k.a., single-season) occupancy model ? In that case, a random effect on occupancy is not identifiable. No replication there to estimate anything, only in detection.

Best regards  -- Marc

From: hmec...@googlegroups.com <hmec...@googlegroups.com> on behalf of Matthijs Hollanders <matthijs....@gmail.com>
Sent: Monday, May 15, 2023 23:51
To: hmecology: Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology <hmec...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: Random site effect on occupancy blowing up
 
Hi all,

I was demonstrating occupancy models in nimble for a colleague and simulated an occupancy model with one site covariate on occupancy and one site-by-survey covariate on detection. Then I added a random site effect to occupancy for demonstration and I noticed that the SD of the random effect was getting overestimated. I added more sites and surveys (went from 50/5 to 200/15) and the problem just seemed to get worse (see attached plot).

I'm wondering if I just misspecified something but I can't see what it would be. Could someone else take a look? Or is this a known issue with occupancy models?

Cheers,

Matt

Hey Marc,

I thought I had deleted the post but clearly not, it was a simple mistake I made due to trying to be clever with having long format data. I left the z[i] in long format too so that I was estimating occupancy for each observation... my bad.

Cheers,

Matt
